findings.claim: Alongside the ordinary inheritance picture of a person who dies and leaves property behind, this ayah also makes the claimant and his voiced claim pass beyond his control, then shows him appearing without the relations or goods on which that claim depended.
findings.mechanism: The inheritance form carries a transfer with the claimant as object; مَا يَقُولُ supplies speech as inherited content; وَيَأْتِينَا moves the claimant to the fixed endpoint; فَرْدًا makes his solitary condition the result.
findings.reader_payoff: The familiar estate image remains, while the sequence also turns the claimant and his words into what passes beyond his control.
findings.containment: This attributed convergence preserves the ordinary inheritance picture and the ordinary transfer, speech, arrival, and solitude readings; it does not claim that the focus itself states a death scene or a human legal estate.

epistemic.reason: The synthesis comes from a legacy_unbound trace, but its focus words, roots, branches, and returns match supplied surface and trusted local analyses.

findings.title: The claim survives as a separable remainder
findings.claim: What he says remains intelligible as sound attached to him, while the inheritance construction also lets that content read as a position that outlasts its speaker and is separately exposed as he arrives alone.
findings.mechanism: نَرِثُ lets the claim pass beyond its holder; the القول-as-position trace extends voiced saying into a maintained stance; the focus word فَرْدًا meets the inherited object as an attributed separated-pearl image; وَيَأْتِينَا presents the claimant apart from what persists.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can perceive the claim and its claimant as separable: the position remains available for account while the person arrives unsupported.
findings.containment: This is an attributed analogy and contextual reading. The Arabic still says that he comes alone; it does not literally name a pearl, string, or detachable physical object.

epistemic.reason: The branch-to-claim synthesis comes from a legacy_unbound trace; focus coordinates and the inheritance, speech, arrival, and solitude relations match supplied evidence, while the pearl remains attributed.
